prize_parts.citation: for establishing induced proximity to an E3 ubiquitin ligase as a designable chemical principle for targeted protein degradation, through PROTAC heterobifunctional degraders and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-class molecular glues

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B036 as a single achievement, credited to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The test I apply is whether the work is a game-changer with demonstrated consequences. Here a simple, general principle (a small molecule brings a chosen protein to an E3 ligase and the cell's own proteasome machinery does the rest) has been reproduced by very many independent groups, is structurally confirmed in ternary complexes, and has opened targets that inhibitors could not reach. Round 1 showed that all eight of us either prefer it or hold it as an alternative, and that the objections concern timing and attribution, not whether the mechanism is real. On the chair's first question I favour one citation on induced proximity covering both PROTACs and glues. The two lines meet at the same E3-ligase mechanism, and cereblon is the link, since it is both the target of thalidomide-class glues and one of the two ligases most used by PROTACs. On the third name, I keep Handa. Cereblon is the discovery that made the glue mechanism understandable and gave the field a widely used ligase handle. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are important, but they are the step that made the concept drug-like, and I count that as development of an established principle. The three-person limit forces that cut, and I name it openly as a cost.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved, to my knowledge, so the practical payoff is still arriving, and I do not want the citation to read as honouring a clinical pipeline. The one-achievement framing is also open to the objection that PROTACs and glues were found at different times by different people, which leaves the glue half resting on a single mechanistic discovery. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito all have real claims, and Ciulli in particular is a defensible third name. If the majority will not accept a prize before clinical approval, B023 is the better-matured alternative, and I would accept that outcome. B034 is the other alternative: it is clean and mature, but the 2010 coupling prize reduces my enthusiasm.

responses.point: If Handa is chosen, the glue half of the citation rests on one mechanistic discovery while the PROTAC half is shared by two people, which is lopsided as a single achievement.
responses.response: That is a fair criticism and the strongest argument for Ciulli as the third name. I still land on Handa, for two reasons. The achievement is the principle, not a count of papers per half, and cereblon connects the glue and bifunctional lines, since it is the ligase that thalidomide-class glues act through and one that many PROTACs engage. And Ciulli's work, however valuable, mostly turned a proven concept into better drugs and structures, whereas Handa's identification of cereblon explained a mechanism that had been a mystery for decades. I would accept Ciulli over Handa only if the committee limits the citation to PROTACs, and I do not think that is the better citation.

responses.point: You asked whether the folding funnel picture has made predictions that experiments later confirmed in a way that sets it apart from the broader physical picture of folding.
responses.response: It has. The funnel picture predicted that fast, minimally frustrated folding is the norm and gave a quantitative route to folding rates and transition-state structure, and Fersht's protein engineering experiments tested exactly those quantities. That is why I keep B023 as an alternative. It does not move me above B036, because the case rests on a theoretical framework intertwined with decades of refinement, and the credit is hard to divide among Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson, Dill and Fersht in three names. We seem to agree that the degradation case is ready and that its weakness is attribution, not science.

responses.point: You ask why folding is not overshadowed by the 2024 protein structure and design prize.
responses.response: The 2024 prize rewarded predicting and designing structures, which is a different question from why proteins fold at all and how fast. The funnel picture answers the second question, and the 2024 recognition does not cover it. I concede that the committee may still feel the neighbouring ground was just visited, and that is a real reason for B023 being my fallback and not my first choice. On your first choice, B014, I agree the in vivo condensate debate does not undermine the reconstituted-system principle. My remaining problem is that the exclusion of Pappu and Mittag takes away the most chemical part of the story, and I have not yet seen the chemistry carry the citation.

responses.point: Kosugi's stannyl-amide coupling was stoichiometric in tin and limited in scope, and the step that made C-N coupling general was the catalytic tin-free system by Buchwald and Hartwig.
responses.response: That answers my question about Kosugi well enough for me. I accept that a citation can acknowledge the antecedent without a laureate slot, so B034 would be a clean two-person prize. My reservation about novelty relative to the 2010 coupling prize stays, since this is a refinement of a paradigm already honoured. I would rate B034 above B014 and below B036 for that reason. If B036 cannot reach five, B034 is where I would look first.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the absence of an approved PROTAC drug as a reason to defer, and what practical impact the expert report would need to show.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name beside Crews and Deshaies, and whether one induced-proximity citation holds up against the objection that PROTACs and glues are two achievements.
Whether B036 can reach five votes, or whether the committee will split between B014 and B034 and leave no majority.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal issue arises for me on any shortlisted candidate. My Warshel/EVB and ribosome work is unrelated to B036, and I have no personal or institutional tie to any credited name. I note the Round 1 disclosures by others and see nothing that changes my view.
